title: SparseBitMatrix Cuthill-McKee row reorder
description:
## Current

No bandwidth-minimization preprocessing for sparse matrices. LDPC parity-check matrices in `gf2-coding` have irregular row spans that hurt cache reuse during repeated matvecs.

## Fix

V7 layout-only: implement Cuthill-McKee (or reverse Cuthill-McKee, RCM) row/column permutation. Apply once before dispatch; amortises across many matvecs.

API: `SparseBitMatrix::reorder_rcm() -> (SparseBitMatrix, RowPermutation)` so callers can recover the original row order on output.

## Per-kernel execution protocol

Per A1's protocol. The "speedup" here is measured by repeatedly applying matvec on the reordered vs. original matrix — single-call measurement is dominated by the reorder cost.

## Depends on

I1, I2, I3, I4.

## Success criteria

- [hard] Reordered + permuted result is bit-exact to original CSR matvec.
- [hard] Permutation roundtrip (apply then unapply) is identity.
- [hard] Bench measures **amortised** matvec cost over ≥ 100 calls.
- [aspirational] ≥1.5× amortised geomean on LDPC parity-check matrix sizes.
